title: Comparing Two Groups with Dot Plots and Box Plots
seo_title: Grade 7 Comparing Data with Dot Plots and Box Plots Worksheets (TEKS 7.12A, STAAR)
standard_text: 7.12A compare two groups of numeric data using comparative dot plots or box plots by comparing their shapes, centers, and spreads
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 worksheets for Texas TEKS 7.12A: compare two groups with medians, IQR, double box plots and dot plots, and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: A narrow box means the middle half is close together.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • To compare two groups, look at shape, center and spread.
  • Center: compare the medians (or means).
  • Spread: compare the IQRs (Q3 − Q1) and ranges.
  • On a double box plot, both groups share one number line, so you can compare them at a glance.

Examples

Example

Class A median 75, IQR 10; Class B median 82, IQR 6

B has the higher center

B is less spread out

Answer: Class B scored higher and more consistently

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Comparing the maximums instead of the centersCompare the medians first.
Using the range for the middle halfThe middle half is the box: use the IQR.
Mixing up the groupsRead the label next to each box.

faq.a: Compare two groups of numeric data using comparative dot plots or box plots by comparing their shapes, centers and spreads.
The median shows a typical value and is not pulled by outliers.

faq.q: What does a narrow box mean?
faq.a: The middle half of the data is close together.

faq.q: Can two groups have the same median but different spreads?
faq.a: Yes. One group can be much more spread out.

items.q: Find the median of 3, 9, 5, 7, 1.
items.e: Order them: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. The middle value is 5.

items.q: Find the median of 12, 4, 8, 10, 6, 2.
items.e: Order them: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. The middle value is 7.
Order them: 11, 13, 15, 17, 19, 21, 23. The middle value is 17.

items.q: Find the median of 40, 25, 30, 35, 45, 50.
items.e: Order them: 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50. The middle value is 37.5.

items.q: Find the median of 7, 2, 9, 4, 6, 8, 3, 5.
items.e: Order them: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. The middle value is 5.5.
Order them: 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28. The middle value is 22.

items.q: The data in order are 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
items.e: Q1 (middle of the lower half) = 4.5. Q3 (middle of the upper half) = 11. IQR = 11 − 4.5 = 6.5. Not 12: that is the range.

items.q: The data in order are 10, 12, 15, 16, 18, 20, 25. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
items.e: Q1 (middle of the lower half) = 12. Q3 (middle of the upper half) = 20. IQR = 20 − 12 = 8. Not 15: that is the range.

items.q: The data in order are 1, 3, 3, 6, 7, 9, 11, 12. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
items.e: Q1 (middle of the lower half) = 3. Q3 (middle of the upper half) = 10. IQR = 10 − 3 = 7. Not 11: that is the range.

items.q: The data in order are 20, 22, 25, 28, 30, 31, 35, 40, 42. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
items.e: Q1 (middle of the lower half) = 23.5. Q3 (middle of the upper half) = 37.5. IQR = 37.5 − 23.5 = 14. Not 22: that is the range.

items.q: The data in order are 5, 6, 8, 10, 11, 13, 15, 16. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
items.e: Q1 (middle of the lower half) = 7. Q3 (middle of the upper half) = 14. IQR = 14 − 7 = 7. Not 11: that is the range.

items.q: The data in order are 30, 32, 35, 36, 40, 44, 45, 50. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
items.e: Q1 (middle of the lower half) = 33.5. Q3 (middle of the upper half) = 44.5. IQR = 44.5 − 33.5 = 11. Not 20: that is the range.

items.q: The data in order are 4, 7, 8, 10, 14, 15, 17, 20. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
items.e: Q1 (middle of the lower half) = 7.5. Q3 (middle of the upper half) = 16. IQR = 16 − 7.5 = 8.5. Not 16: that is the range.

items.q: What does the IQR measure?
c: The spread of the middle half of the data
items.e: IQR = Q3 − Q1, the width of the middle 50%.

items.q: Which measure of center is better when there is an outlier?
items.e: The median is not pulled by extreme values.

items.q: Which pair goes together?
items.e: Use median with IQR, and mean with MAD.

items.q: A box plot shows Q1 = 12, median = 15 and Q3 = 20. What is the IQR?
In a box plot, the box shows…
items.e: The box goes from Q1 to Q3.

items.q: A data set is 2, 3, 3, 4, 40. Why is the median a better center than the mean?
c: 40 is an outlier that pulls the mean up
items.e: The mean is 10.4, larger than 4 of the 5 values. The median, 3, fits the data better.

items.q: Adding a very large value to a data set changes which measure more?
items.e: Every value is in the mean, so one large value pulls it a lot. The median moves little.

items.q: Group A: Class A test scores: 70, 75, 80, 85, 90. Group B: Class B test scores: 78, 80, 82, 84, 86. Compare the means.
c: Group A has the greater mean because it has the largest value
Group A has the greater mean (82 vs 80)
Group B has the greater mean (82 vs 80)

items.q: Group A: 70, 75, 80, 85, 90. Group B: 78, 80, 82, 84, 86. Which group's data are more spread out (larger MAD)?
items.e: MAD A = 6 and MAD B = 2.4.

items.q: Group A: Team A heights (in.): 58, 60, 62, 64, 66. Group B: Team B heights (in.): 62, 64, 66, 68, 70. Compare the means.
c: Group A has the greater mean because it has the largest value
Group A has the greater mean (66 vs 62)
Group B has the greater mean (66 vs 62)

items.q: Group A: 58, 60, 62, 64, 66. Group B: 62, 64, 66, 68, 70. Which group's data are more spread out (larger MAD)?
items.e: MAD A = 2.4 and MAD B = 2.4.

items.q: Group A: Store A prices ($): 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. Group B: Store B prices ($): 7, 8, 8, 9, 13. Compare the means.
c: Group B has the greater mean (9 vs 8)
Group A has the greater mean (9 vs 8)
Group A has the greater mean because it has the largest value

items.q: Group A: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. Group B: 7, 8, 8, 9, 13. Which group's data are more spread out (larger MAD)?
items.e: MAD A = 2.4 and MAD B = 1.6.

items.q: Group A: Plant A heights (cm): 10, 12, 13, 15, 20. Group B: Plant B heights (cm): 11, 11, 14, 16, 18. Compare the means.
c: Group A has the greater mean (14 vs 14)
Group B has the greater mean (14 vs 14)
Group A has the greater mean because it has the largest value

items.q: Group A: 10, 12, 13, 15, 20. Group B: 11, 11, 14, 16, 18. Which group's data are more spread out (larger MAD)?
items.e: MAD A = 2.8 and MAD B = 2.4.

items.q: Two groups have means 80 and 85. Both have a MAD of 5. How many MADs apart are the means?
items.e: Difference of means = 5. 5 ÷ 5 = 1 MADs.

items.q: Two groups have means 62 and 68. Both have a MAD of 3. How many MADs apart are the means?
items.e: Difference of means = 6. 6 ÷ 3 = 2 MADs.

items.q: Two groups have means 40 and 46. Both have a MAD of 2. How many MADs apart are the means?
items.e: Difference of means = 6. 6 ÷ 2 = 3 MADs.

items.q: Two groups have means 100 and 112. Both have a MAD of 4. How many MADs apart are the means?
items.e: Difference of means = 12. 12 ÷ 4 = 3 MADs.

items.q: Two groups have means 25 and 27. Both have a MAD of 4. How many MADs apart are the means?
items.e: Difference of means = 2. 2 ÷ 4 = 0.5 MADs.

items.q: Two groups have means 150 and 165. Both have a MAD of 5. How many MADs apart are the means?
items.e: Difference of means = 15. 15 ÷ 5 = 3 MADs.

items.q: Two groups have means 50 and 53. Both have a MAD of 1. How many MADs apart are the means?
items.e: Difference of means = 3. 3 ÷ 1 = 3 MADs.

items.q: Two groups have means 70 and 79. Both have a MAD of 3. How many MADs apart are the means?
items.e: Difference of means = 9. 9 ÷ 3 = 3 MADs.

items.q: Two groups have means 12 and 16. Both have a MAD of 2. How many MADs apart are the means?
items.e: Difference of means = 4. 4 ÷ 2 = 2 MADs.

items.q: Two groups have means 90 and 99. Both have a MAD of 6. How many MADs apart are the means?
items.e: Difference of means = 9. 9 ÷ 6 = 1.5 MADs.

items.q: The means of two groups are 1 MAD apart. What does this suggest?
c: The groups do not overlap at all
items.e: The more MADs apart the centers are, the less the groups overlap. About 2 or more MADs suggests a real difference.

items.q: The means of two groups are 4 MADs apart. What does this suggest?
c: The groups are almost the same
The groups are very different with little overlap
items.e: The more MADs apart the centers are, the less the groups overlap. About 2 or more MADs suggests a real difference.

A dot plot shows most values between 20 and 30, with one value at 70. Which measures best describe it?
items.e: Center (mean, median) tells a typical value. Spread (MAD, IQR, range) tells how much values vary.

items.q: A dot plot is symmetric with no outliers. Which measures fit well?
items.e: Center (mean, median) tells a typical value. Spread (MAD, IQR, range) tells how much values vary.

items.q: Two dot plots have the same center, but one is much wider. What is different?
items.e: Center (mean, median) tells a typical value. Spread (MAD, IQR, range) tells how much values vary.

items.q: Two box plots have the same IQR, but one is shifted 10 units to the right. What is different?
items.e: Center (mean, median) tells a typical value. Spread (MAD, IQR, range) tells how much values vary.

items.q: Seventh graders' reaction times have median 0.32 s, and eighth graders' have median 0.28 s, with similar IQRs. Which inference is reasonable?
c: Eighth graders tend to react a bit faster
items.e: Center (mean, median) tells a typical value. Spread (MAD, IQR, range) tells how much values vary.

items.q: Random samples of 7th and 8th graders' sleep: means 8.2 h and 7.6 h, MAD 0.6 h each. How many MADs apart are the means?
items.e: Center (mean, median) tells a typical value. Spread (MAD, IQR, range) tells how much values vary.

Same mean; B is more spread out

Same center; B is more spread out
